newsitem.title: USA: Circus Circus unveils plan for new resort.
newsitem.headline: Circus Circus unveils plan for new resort.

text.p: Circus Circus Enterprises Inc. unveiled plans Tuesday to build a 4,000-room resort casino modelled on a South Sea island in Las Vegas, starting with the planned destruction of the Hacienda Hotel on New Year's Eve.

The Hacienda, which is to be blown up on national television, sits on the site along Vegas' famed "Strip" where the resort for upscale tourists and high-rolling gamblers that is code-named Project Paradise, will be built.
The resort will attempt to recreate a South Seas island and will include jungle foliage, waterfalls and terraced gardens, the Las Vegas-based company said in a statement.
At its centre will be a wave-washed beach, reef and tropical fish among which visitors can snorkle. Next to that will be a shark-filled tank they can swim by.

"This will be the lushest property we've done and, our sense is, the most extensive resort design in Las Vegas," Glenn Schaeffer, Circus Circus president and chief financial officer, said in an interview.

Construction is slated to start in February and end in fall of 1998. Schaeffer declined to give an exact cost estimate for the project, saying some infrastructure decisions must be made before a final budget is announced.

Financial analysts and published reports have put the cost anywhere between $700 million and $1 billion, and he said that range would be a safe estimate. The project will be financed through cash flow and bank lines of credit.

A recent research report from investment firm Salomon Brothers forecast earnings before interest, taxes and depreciation and amortization, or cash flow, of $136 million in the Project Paradise's first full year of operation.
"We would expect a higher figure than that," Schaeffer said, though he declined to forecast an exact return.
The company owns and operates 10 properties in Nevada, including the themed Circus Circus, Excalibur and Luxor hotels and casinos in Las Vegas.
Circus Circus stock closed 37.5 cents lower at $34.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
